```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod_h <- readModelDb("Zhang_2026_SYHA1805_human")
mod_m <- readModelDb("Zhang_2026_SYHA1805_monkey")
ui_h <- rxode2::rxode(mod_h)
ui_m <- rxode2::rxode(mod_m)
```

* Citation: `r ui_h$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18070862>
* Full text and supplement:
  <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13414496/>

SYHA1805 is a non-steroidal farnesoid X receptor (FXR) agonist in development
for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Zhang 2026
combines in vitro ADME work, rat and cynomolgus monkey pharmacokinetics,
allometric scaling and Simcyp (version 20) physiologically based
pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models of rat, monkey and human to choose the
first-in-human dose. It then checks the human model against a
single-ascending-dose (SAD) study (CTR20202354) at 30, 60 and 120 mg.

A literature check on 2026-11-15 (Europe PMC search for "SYHA1805") found no
erratum or correction for the paper.

# What these models are, and what they are not

The three PBPK models use Simcyp's full-PBPK distribution model with
Rodgers-Rowland ("method 2") tissue:plasma partition coefficients and a
`Kp` scalar. Simcyp's whole-body mass-balance equations, its organ volumes and
blood flows, and the resulting tissue `Kp` values are platform outputs that
the paper does not print, so the platform models themselves cannot be
rebuilt. What Table 3 does print, per species, is the drug layer: the in vivo
intravenous clearance input, the predicted steady-state volume `Vss`,
first-order absorption (`ka`, fraction absorbed `fa`), the blood-to-plasma
ratio and `fu`.

For the human and the monkey models that is enough for a one-compartment
reduction with no fitted parameter. Oral bioavailability is the product
`fa * Fg * Fh`. Elimination is a single in vivo clearance with no gut-wall
term, so `Fg = 1`; `Fh` follows from the well-stirred liver,
`Fh = 1 - CL / (Qh * B/P)`, using the hepatic blood flows the paper itself
uses for allometry (Supplementary Equation S10: 1450 mL/min for a human,
122.5 mL/min for the monkey) and `B/P = 1.00` (Table 3). The paper's own
model predictions are the answer key: Figure 4 (human predicted AUC and
Cmax), Figure 5 (human predicted mean profile and 90% interval) and
Figure 3D-F (monkey predicted AUC, CL and Cmax). The maintainers digitised
those figures from the publisher's high-resolution images; the values are
typed into the chunks below.

```{r f-derivation}
qh_h <- 1450 * 60 / 1000   # L/h, human hepatic blood flow (Eq. S10)
qh_m <- 122.5 * 60 / 1000  # L/h, monkey hepatic blood flow (Eq. S10)
cl_h <- 20.7               # L/h, Table 3 (human column; see Errata)
cl_m <- 23.46 * 60 / 1000  # L/h, Table 3 (monkey)
bp <- 1.00                 # Table 3, all species

f_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Species = c("Human", "Cynomolgus monkey"),
  fa = c(1.00, 0.02),
  Fh = c(1 - cl_h / (qh_h * bp), 1 - cl_m / (qh_m * bp))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(F = fa * Fh)

knitr::kable(f_tab |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 4))),
             caption = "Oral bioavailability derived from printed values (Fg = 1).")

stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(exp(ui_h$theta[["lfdepot"]]), f_tab$F[1], tolerance = 1e-3)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(exp(ui_m$theta[["lfdepot"]]), f_tab$F[2], tolerance = 1e-3))
)
```

## Why the rat model is not reproduced

The rat model has the same drug layer (CL 16.99 mL/min, `Vss` 1.85 L/kg,
`ka` 0.30 1/h, `fa` 1.00), but its bioavailability cannot be derived from
printed values. The rat clearance input exceeds the rat hepatic blood flow
the paper prints (11.8 mL/min, Supplementary Equation S10), which would make
the hepatic extraction ratio greater than one:

```{r rat-check}
c(rat_CL_mL_min = 16.99, rat_Qh_mL_min = 11.8, extraction_ratio = 16.99 / 11.8)
stopifnot(16.99 / 11.8 > 1)
```

Simcyp must therefore have used its own rat blood flows or an extra
systemic clearance, neither of which is printed, so the oral rat arm rests on
an unprinted platform output. The intravenous rat arm alone would be checked
only against its predicted AUC and clearance (Figure 3A-B), which equal
`dose / CL` for any model with that clearance and so test nothing about the
reduction. The rat layer is documented here and not packaged.

# Population

```{r population}
pop_row <- function(p) {
  c(p$species, p$n_subjects, p$age_range, p$weight_median,
    p$sex_female_pct, p$disease_state, p$dose_range)
}
pop_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Field = c("Species", "Subjects", "Age", "Weight", "% female", "Disease",
            "Doses"),
  Human = pop_row(ui_h$population),
  Monkey = pop_row(ui_m$population)
)
knitr::kable(pop_tab, caption = "Populations behind the two reductions.")
```

The human PBPK simulations used a Simcyp virtual population of 10 trials of
10 healthy volunteers (n = 100, half female, 20-50 years; section 2.6.2),
and were compared with the SAD study CTR20202354 in healthy Chinese
volunteers sampled to 72 h. The monkey model was built and checked on
24 cynomolgus monkeys (4 groups of 6, 3 per sex) given 1 mg/kg
intravenously or 10, 30 or 100 mg/kg orally (section 2.3.2, Table 2).

# Source trace

```{r source-trace}
trace_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Model,   ~Parameter, ~Value,       ~Source,
  "human",  "lka",      "0.30 1/h",   "Table 3 'ka (1/h)', Oral (Human)",
  "human",  "lcl",      "20.7 L/h",   "Table 3 'CLi.v', Oral (Human) 20.70; abstract and section 3.4 '20.7 L/h'; Table S7 monkey-based mean",
  "human",  "lvc",      "14.7 L",     "Table 3 'Vss' Predicted (0.21 L/kg) x 70 kg (section 3.4 reference weight)",
  "human",  "lfdepot",  "0.7621",     "fa 1.00 (Table 3) x Fg 1 x Fh = 1 - 20.7 / (87.0 x 1.00); Qh 1450 mL/min (Eq. S10), B/P 1.00 (Table 3)",
  "human",  "propSd",   "0 (fixed)",  "No residual-error model reported",
  "monkey", "lka",      "0.30 1/h",   "Table 3 'ka (1/h)', Oral (Monkey)",
  "monkey", "lcl",      "1.4076 L/h", "Table 3 'CLi.v (mL/min)' 23.46, Monkey; = 8.35 mL/min/kg (Table 2) x 2.81 kg",
  "monkey", "lvc",      "0.6463 L",   "Table 3 'Vss' Predicted (0.23 L/kg) x 2.81 kg",
  "monkey", "lfdepot",  "0.01617",    "fa 0.02 (Table 3) x Fg 1 x Fh = 1 - 23.46 / (122.5 x 1.00); Qh 122.5 mL/min (Eq. S10)",
  "monkey", "propSd",   "0 (fixed)",  "No residual-error model reported"
)
knitr::kable(trace_tab, caption = "Source trace for every fixed parameter.")
```

Both models are the standard one-compartment first-order-absorption system
(`d/dt(depot) = -ka * depot`, `d/dt(central) = ka * depot - kel * central`,
`kel = cl / vc`, `f(depot) = F`, `Cc = 1000 * central / vc`) with no
nonstandard terms. The `1000` converts mg/L to ng/mL.

The 2.81 kg monkey weight is not printed but is implied twice by the paper's
own numbers, so it is not an assumption of the maintainers:

```{r monkey-weight}
bw_from_cl <- 23.46 / 8.35  # Table 3 mL/min / Table 2 mL/min/kg
bw_from_qh <- 122.5 / 43.6  # Eq. S10 mL/min / Table S1 mL/min/kg
c(bw_from_cl = bw_from_cl, bw_from_qh = bw_from_qh)
stopifnot(abs(bw_from_cl - 2.81) < 0.01, abs(bw_from_qh - 2.81) < 0.01)
```

# Virtual cohort

Both models have no random effects, so they are deterministic and one
subject fully describes each regimen. Human regimens are the SAD doses of
30, 60 and 120 mg. Monkey regimens are 1 mg/kg intravenous (a bolus into
`central`) and 10, 30 and 100 mg/kg oral (into `depot`), converted to mg at
2.81 kg. Observations sit on the `central` ODE state, where `Cc` is returned
as an algebraic observable.

```{r cohort}
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.01), seq(2, 72, by = 0.05))))

make_events <- function(id, amt, cmt, arm) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(id = id, time = 0, amt = amt, evid = 1L, cmt = cmt,
                   arm = arm),
    tibble::tibble(id = id, time = obs_grid, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L,
                   cmt = "central", arm = arm)
  )
}

bw_m <- 2.81
ev_h <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(1L, 30, "depot", "30 mg"),
  make_events(2L, 60, "depot", "60 mg"),
  make_events(3L, 120, "depot", "120 mg")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

ev_m <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(1L, 1 * bw_m, "central", "IV 1 mg/kg"),
  make_events(2L, 10 * bw_m, "depot", "Oral 10 mg/kg"),
  make_events(3L, 30 * bw_m, "depot", "Oral 30 mg/kg"),
  make_events(4L, 100 * bw_m, "depot", "Oral 100 mg/kg")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_h[, c("id", "time", "evid")]),
          !anyDuplicated(ev_m[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim_h <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h, events = ev_h, keep = "arm",
                         rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_m <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_m, events = ev_m, keep = "arm",
                         rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(all(is.finite(sim_h$Cc)), all(is.finite(sim_m$Cc)),
          length(unique(sim_h$id)) == 3L, length(unique(sim_m$id)) == 4L)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 5: human predicted profiles

Figure 5 shows, for each SAD dose, the PBPK model's predicted **mean**
profile (orange), its 90% interval (purple) and the observed means, on a
log scale from 1e-20 to 1e5 ng/mL. The table below holds the maintainers'
digitised values: the predicted mean curve over 0.5-12 h (where it is not
hidden behind the observed points), and the geometric centre of the 90%
interval (the midpoint in log space of its 5th and 95th percentile edges) at
16-47 h.

```{r fig5-digitised}
fig5_mean <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,     ~time, ~log10_mean,
  "30 mg",  0.5,   2.15,
  "30 mg",  1,     2.23,
  "30 mg",  2,     2.29,
  "30 mg",  3.5,   2.11,
  "30 mg",  5.5,   1.89,
  "30 mg",  8,     1.63,
  "30 mg",  12,    1.17,
  "60 mg",  0.5,   2.45,
  "60 mg",  1,     2.55,
  "60 mg",  2,     2.55,
  "60 mg",  3.5,   2.45,
  "60 mg",  5.5,   2.23,
  "120 mg", 0.5,   2.75,
  "120 mg", 1,     2.83,
  "120 mg", 2,     2.89,
  "120 mg", 3.5,   2.73,
  "120 mg", 5.5,   2.51,
  "120 mg", 8,     2.31,
  "120 mg", 12,    1.85
)
fig5_band <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,     ~time, ~log10_p95, ~log10_p5,
  "30 mg",  16,    1.16,       -0.40,
  "30 mg",  24,    0.60,       -1.89,
  "30 mg",  36,    -0.24,      -4.10,
  "30 mg",  47,    -1.04,      -6.14,
  "60 mg",  16,    1.45,       -0.12,
  "60 mg",  24,    0.88,       -1.57,
  "60 mg",  36,    0.08,       -3.82,
  "60 mg",  47,    -0.76,      -5.82,
  "120 mg", 16,    1.77,       0.20,
  "120 mg", 24,    1.20,       -1.29,
  "120 mg", 36,    0.36,       -3.49,
  "120 mg", 47,    -0.48,      -5.54
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(log10_centre = (log10_p95 + log10_p5) / 2)

model_at <- function(sim, a, t) {
  vapply(seq_along(t), function(i) {
    sim$Cc[sim$arm == a[i] & abs(sim$time - t[i]) < 1e-8]
  }, numeric(1))
}

chk_mean <- fig5_mean |>
  dplyr::mutate(log10_model = log10(model_at(sim_h, arm, time)),
                diff = log10_model - log10_mean)
chk_band <- fig5_band |>
  dplyr::mutate(log10_model = log10(model_at(sim_h, arm, time)),
                diff = log10_model - log10_centre)

knitr::kable(chk_mean |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
               dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "Fig 5 mean (log10 ng/mL)" = log10_mean,
                             "Reduction (log10 ng/mL)" = log10_model,
                             "Difference (decades)" = diff),
             caption = "Reduction vs. the digitised Figure 5 predicted mean, 0.5-12 h (gated to 5.5 h).")
knitr::kable(chk_band |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
               dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "95th pct" = log10_p95, "5th pct" = log10_p5,
                             "Centre" = log10_centre, "Reduction" = log10_model,
                             "Difference (decades)" = diff),
             caption = "Reduction vs. the geometric centre of the digitised Figure 5 90% interval, 16-47 h (log10 ng/mL).")

# Digitising error is about 0.04 decades; 0.15 decades (41%) on the early
# mean and 0.25 decades on the band centre leave room for that and for the
# platform's population averaging, while a wrong clearance, volume, ka or F
# moves these curves by far more.
# The early-mean check covers absorption and the peak (to 5.5 h). From about
# 8 h the platform's population mean starts to sit above any single typical
# profile (see the narrative below), so those rows are shown but not gated.
early <- chk_mean$time <= 5.5
stopifnot(sum(early) == 15L,
          max(abs(chk_mean$diff[early])) < 0.15,
          max(abs(chk_band$diff)) < 0.25)
```

```{r figure-5, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(dplyr::filter(sim_h, time <= 48),
       aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = fig5_mean, aes(time, 10^log10_mean, colour = "Figure 5 predicted mean"),
             size = 2) +
  geom_point(data = fig5_band, aes(time, 10^log10_centre, colour = "Figure 5 90% interval centre"),
             size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(arm, levels = c("30 mg", "60 mg", "120 mg"))) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma SYHA1805 (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Zhang 2026 (line: reduction; points: digitised PBPK predictions).") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The reduction follows the predicted mean to within 0.1 decade (25%) through
absorption and the peak, to 5.5 h. From about 8 h the mean starts to run
above it (by 0.05-0.13 decade at 8 h and 0.11-0.19 decade at 12 h), and later
the platform's **arithmetic mean** curve flattens (to about 0.04 ng/mL at 48 h
after 30 mg), but its 90% interval widens to five decades: by 47 h the
5th and 95th percentiles are 1e-6 and 0.1 ng/mL. A mean over subjects whose
exponential decline rates differ is dominated by the slowest subjects, so the
flat tail is a property of the averaging, not of a typical subject. The
reduction is a typical subject, and it runs through the centre of the
interval at every late time.

## Figure 3D-F: monkey predicted AUC and Cmax

Figure 3 labels its axes in ng/mL, but its observed coordinates are the
nmol/L values of Table 2 (for example the oral 10 mg/kg AUC sits at
564 against Table 2's AUC0-last of 564 nM*h, and the oral Cmax at 144 against
143 nM). The predicted values are therefore read in nmol/L too.

```{r fig3-digitised}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,             ~dose_mgkg, ~auc_pred_nM, ~cmax_pred_nM, ~auc_obs_nM, ~cmax_obs_nM,
  "IV 1 mg/kg",     1,          3590,         NA,            3600,        NA,
  "Oral 10 mg/kg",  10,         563,          120,           669,         143,
  "Oral 30 mg/kg",  30,         1652,         361,           1440,        319,
  "Oral 100 mg/kg", 100,        6026,         1062,          3640,        633
)
knitr::kable(fig3, caption = paste("Digitised Figure 3D/3F predictions with Table 2",
                                   "observed AUC0-inf and Cmax (nM*h, nM)."))
```

The first comparison needs no molecular weight. For a linear model the
dose-normalised ratio of oral to intravenous AUC is the bioavailability, so
the platform's own predictions imply an `F` that can be set against the one
derived from the printed `fa`, `CL` and `Qh`:

```{r monkey-f-check}
auc_iv_per_mgkg <- fig3$auc_pred_nM[1] / fig3$dose_mgkg[1]
f_chk <- fig3 |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_mgkg > 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(F_implied = auc_pred_nM / dose_mgkg / auc_iv_per_mgkg,
                F_model = exp(ui_m$theta[["lfdepot"]]),
                pct = 100 * (F_model / F_implied - 1))
knitr::kable(f_chk |> dplyr::select(arm, F_implied, F_model, pct) |>
               dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
               dplyr::rename("F implied by Figure 3D" = F_implied, "F in model" = F_model,
                             "% diff" = pct),
             caption = "Monkey oral bioavailability: model vs. platform predictions.")
stopifnot(max(abs(f_chk$pct)) < 10)
```

Taking `fa = 0.02` alone as the bioavailability would over-predict every oral
AUC by 24% (1 / 0.808); the hepatic first-pass term closes that gap.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
run_nca <- function(sim, ev, route_of) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)
  dose_df <- ev |>
    dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
    dplyr::mutate(route = route_of(cmt)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm, route)
  stopifnot(nrow(conc) > 0, any(conc$time == 0))
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | arm + id,
                               concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id,
                               doseu = "mg", route = "route")
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                          aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"))
}
route_of <- function(cmt) ifelse(cmt == "central", "intravascular", "extravascular")

nca_h <- run_nca(sim_h, ev_h, route_of)
nca_m <- run_nca(sim_m, ev_m, route_of)

knitr::kable(nca_h |> dplyr::mutate(PPORRES = signif(PPORRES, 4)) |>
               dplyr::select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES, PPORRESU),
             caption = "PKNCA results, human reduction.")
knitr::kable(nca_m |> dplyr::mutate(PPORRES = signif(PPORRES, 4)) |>
               dplyr::select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES, PPORRESU),
             caption = "PKNCA results, monkey reduction.")
```

## Closed-form gates

For a linear model `AUCinf = F * dose / CL` exactly, and for a one-compartment
first-order absorption model `Tmax = log(ka / kel) / (ka - kel)`. These check
the NCA set-up as much as the models.

```{r closed-form}
get_nca <- function(nca, a, p) {
  v <- nca$PPORRES[nca$arm == a & nca$PPTESTCD == p]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique NCA row for ", a, " ", p)
  v
}
th_h <- ui_h$theta
kel_h <- exp(th_h[["lcl"]]) / exp(th_h[["lvc"]])
ka_h <- exp(th_h[["lka"]])
gate <- tibble::tibble(
  arm = c("30 mg", "60 mg", "120 mg"),
  dose = c(30, 60, 120)
) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_nca = get_nca(nca_h, arm, "aucinf.obs"),
    auc_cf = exp(th_h[["lfdepot"]]) * dose / exp(th_h[["lcl"]]) * 1000,
    tmax_nca = get_nca(nca_h, arm, "tmax"),
    tmax_cf = log(ka_h / kel_h) / (ka_h - kel_h)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
knitr::kable(gate |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 5))),
             caption = "Human: NCA vs. closed-form AUC0-inf and Tmax.")
# AUC: trapezoidal error on the fine grid only. Tmax: the 0.01 h grid.
stopifnot(max(abs(gate$auc_nca / gate$auc_cf - 1)) < 0.005,
          max(abs(gate$tmax_nca - gate$tmax_cf)) <= 0.011)
```

# Comparison against the published NCA

## Human: against the paper's own PBPK predictions

This comparison decides whether the reduction is faithful to the platform
model. Nothing was tuned to reach these values.

```{r compare-pred-human}
sim_cmp_h <- nca_h |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "cmax")) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
ref_pred_h <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::transmute(arm, aucinf.obs = auc_pred, cmax = cmax_pred)
cmp_h <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_cmp_h, reference = ref_pred_h, by = "arm",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", cmax = "ng/mL"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_h, caption = paste("Human reduction vs. the PBPK predictions digitised",
                                    "from Zhang 2026 Figure 4. * differs by >20%."))
pct_h <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.eE+-]", "", cmp_h[["% diff"]]))
stopifnot(sum(is.finite(pct_h)) == 6L, max(abs(pct_h)) < 20)
```

The predicted AUCs agree to within 3%. Cmax is 7-9% above the platform's
value: its predicted Cmax is a mean over a virtual population whose
individual peaks occur at different times, which lowers it relative to the
peak of a single typical profile (Figure 5's mean curve peaks near
195 ng/mL after 30 mg, the reduction at 218 ng/mL).

## Human: against the observed SAD data

```{r compare-obs-human}
ref_obs_h <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::transmute(arm, aucinf.obs = auc_obs, cmax = cmax_obs)
cmp_h_obs <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_cmp_h, reference = ref_obs_h, by = "arm",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", cmax = "ng/mL"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_h_obs, caption = paste("Human reduction vs. the observed SAD values",
                                        "digitised from Figure 4. * differs by >20%."))
```

The reduction over-predicts the observed SAD exposure, by 1.8-2.0-fold on
AUC and 1.6-1.9-fold on Cmax. The PBPK model does the same (Figure 4: every
point lies near the 2-fold line), and the paper attributes it to the lumped
first-order absorption, which does not capture the dissolution- and
permeability-limited uptake of this poorly soluble P-gp substrate
(Discussion). The model is packaged as published, not adjusted to the
clinical data.

## Monkey: against the paper's own PBPK predictions

Converting the model's ng/mL to nmol/L needs the molecular weight, which the
paper does not print. The maintainers used 583 g/mol, from the protonated
molecular ion of the LC-MS/MS transition (m/z 584.0 -> 266.2, positive
electrospray; section 2.3.2). The intravenous row checks the conversion.

```{r compare-pred-monkey}
mw <- 583
sim_cmp_m <- nca_m |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "cmax")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!(arm == "IV 1 mg/kg" & PPTESTCD == "cmax")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(PPORRES = PPORRES / mw * 1000) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
ref_pred_m <- fig3 |>
  dplyr::transmute(arm, aucinf.obs = auc_pred_nM, cmax = cmax_pred_nM)
cmp_m <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_cmp_m, reference = ref_pred_m, by = "arm",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "nM*h", cmax = "nM"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_m, caption = paste("Monkey reduction vs. the PBPK predictions digitised",
                                    "from Zhang 2026 Figure 3D/3F. * differs by >20%."))
pct_m <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.eE+-]", "", cmp_m[["% diff"]]))
stopifnot(sum(is.finite(pct_m)) == 7L, max(abs(pct_m)) < 20)
```

All AUCs agree to within 9% and the 10 and 30 mg/kg Cmax to within 1%. The
platform's 100 mg/kg point sits slightly off its own linear trend (its
dose-normalised AUC is 7% above, and its dose-normalised Cmax 12% below, the
10 mg/kg values), which a linear reduction cannot follow.

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_df <- sim_cmp_m |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(ref_pred_m, -arm, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "pred"),
    by = c("arm", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(pred)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(PPTESTCD = dplyr::recode(PPTESTCD, aucinf.obs = "AUC (nM*h)", cmax = "Cmax (nM)"))
ggplot(plot_df, aes(pred, PPORRES, shape = arm)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = log10(c(0.8, 1.25)), colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ PPTESTCD, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "PBPK prediction (Figure 3D/3F)", y = "Reduction", shape = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3D and 3F of Zhang 2026 against the reduction (lines: 1, 0.8 and 1.25-fold).") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Model class.** Both files are one-compartment reductions of Simcyp
  full-PBPK models, not the platform models. Organ volumes, blood flows and
  tissue `Kp` values are Simcyp outputs the paper does not print. The
  reductions carry the printed clearance and lumped `Vss` and are checked
  against the platform's own predictions above; no parameter was fitted.
* **Bioavailability.** `F = fa * Fg * Fh`, with `Fg = 1` because no gut-wall
  clearance is specified, and `Fh` from the well-stirred liver at the hepatic
  blood flows of Supplementary Equation S10 with all clearance hepatic (no
  renal clearance is printed). Simcyp's own internal blood flows may differ
  slightly from these; the agreement with the platform's predicted AUC
  (within 3% in human, 9% in monkey) bounds the effect.
* **Reference weights.** Human: 70 kg, the paper's allometric reference
  (section 3.4), used to turn `Vss` 0.21 L/kg into 14.7 L (the allometric
  `Vss,h` in the text is 15.1 L). Monkey: 2.81 kg, implied by the paper's
  own clearance and blood-flow numbers (shown above).
* **No variability.** The source reports no inter-individual or residual
  variance; the Simcyp virtual-population spread is a platform output. Both
  models are typical-value models with `propSd` fixed at zero, so they cannot
  reproduce the width of the Figure 5 interval or the tail of its mean curve.
* **Digitised references.** All comparison values come from the maintainers'
  digitisation of Figures 3, 4 and 5 (high-resolution publisher images;
  reading error about 1-2% on the scatter plots and 0.04 decades on
  Figure 5).
* **Molecular weight.** 583 g/mol, from the m/z 584.0 [M+H]+ ion, used only
  to convert monkey concentrations to the nmol/L of Figure 3.
* **Rat model.** Not packaged; its bioavailability is not derivable from
  printed values (see above).

## Errata in the source

* **Table 3, human clearance units.** The `CLi.v (mL/min)` row gives 20.70 for
  the human column. That value is in L/h: the abstract, section 3.4 and
  Supplementary Table S7 all give 20.7 L/h (20.7 mL/min would be 1.24 L/h,
  and could not produce the predicted AUC of Figure 4). The rat (16.99) and
  monkey (23.46) entries are in mL/min as labelled
  (80.9 mL/min/kg x 0.21 kg and 8.35 mL/min/kg x 2.81 kg).
* **Figures 4 and 5, dose units.** The legends read 30, 60 and 120 "mg/kg";
  the SAD doses are 30, 60 and 120 mg (section 3.5: "30 mg was selected as
  the starting dose"), and only mg doses reproduce the predicted AUC.
* **Figure 3, concentration units.** Axes read ng/mL, but the observed
  coordinates match the nmol/L values of Table 2.
* **Absorption in human vs. monkey.** Table 3 gives `fa` 0.02 for the monkey
  but 1.00 for the human, although section 3.5 says the absorption parameters
  were translated from rat to monkey to human. The values are encoded as
  printed; the paper's Discussion notes that the human model over-predicts
  exposure.
